verdict.rationale: Twilio's official MCP server gives AI coding agents structured access to its API surface, but it only indexes public API specifications and needs no account or keys. It therefore helps agents read and write code against the API rather than letting a user operate their Twilio account through natural-language commands. Nothing else in the pack documents a natural-language console, assistant, or command interface for running the product, so this MCP evidence is an adjacent developer building block only.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands
